title: Should ChatGPT be Biased? Challenges and Risks of Bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: The paper is a perspective/survey article and does not conduct original empirical measurements. It conceptually evaluates demographic biases (e.g., gender, race, ethnicity) through a literature review of their origins in training data and their downstream societal risks.
Conceptually evaluated through literature review, focusing on how large language models absorb and perpetuate cultural stereotypes present in vast internet text corpora.
Theoretically analyzed by examining the disparity in model proficiency between dominant internet languages (e.g., English) and low-resource languages or minority dialects.
Evaluated conceptually by assessing the limitations and biases introduced by training data cutoffs and the lack of temporally representative data for current events.
Discussed theoretically by analyzing how models inadvertently reinforce pre-existing beliefs by generating outputs that align with the biased information-seeking behaviors captured in training data.
Conceptually evaluated through literature review to describe how language models learn, favor, and propagate specific political perspectives or ideologies present in their training material.
